key_insight: A mechanism-based constitutive model links dislocation-scale physics to BCC metal plasticity, distinguishing structural resistance from thermal activation and phonon drag.
engineering_relevance: The model supports strength and creep predictions across temperature and strain-rate regimes, including anomalous thermal hardening.
method: Develop a temperature-dependent screw-dislocation mobility law combining thermal activation and relativistic effects.
Run discrete dislocation dynamics tension and compression simulations at different initial dislocation densities.
Derive a unified constitutive model with physical criteria for combining structural and kinetic resistance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports bottom-up simulations that quantify the crossover from thermal activation to phonon-drag-dominated flow, but provides no numerical accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Experimental validation and transferability across specific BCC metals are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Unified constitutive model of body-centered cubic metals informed by discrete dislocation dynamics
